This needs to be tackled by fiscal consolidation to allow interest rates to come down and debt to stabilize over time, we argue. In this report we examine the state of Colombia’s fiscal accounts, look at the possible options for fiscal consolidation over the next year and explore their realistic outcomes. Rather than focusing on election outcomes themselves, investors may want to pay closer attention to the evolution of FX hedging beha viour around political events. Our data suggest that Colombia and Brazil currently sit at opposite ends of the election-positioning cycle. In Colombia, foreign investors appear to be unwinding election-related hedges after the vote. In Brazil, by contrast, hedg e ratios remain unusually low relative to previous election cycles, suggesting investors have yet to meaningfully increase protection against election risk. The strike map then sums all one-day notionals in a given strike bucket (e.g in the 1.1800-1.1850 range in EURUSD), presenting an estimate of approximate options positioning around prevailing spot rates. Positioning is like a risk reversal: In general, we find that strike map gamma positioning can indicate likely spot-vol correlations: spot moving away from owned-gamma is typically positive vol, spot moving towards the centre of the options distribution is typically negative vol. In other words, positioning can act like a risk reversal indicator and a larger positioning score can indicate stronger spot-vol correlation. EURUSD and USDJPY exhibit positioning-driven vol behaviour most strongly. Directionally the behaviour is consistent in G10 pairs but sensitivity is lower in GBPUSD, AUDUSD, and USDCAD, particularly on the USD-weaker side of the positioning distribution (when spot is above median for GBP and AUD; spot below median for USDCAD). This could reflect the dollar-vol heuristic (see FX vol: The dollar- vol heuristic, dated 1 February 2023) where we find that implied vols for high-beta currencies tend to be most sensitive to USD performance: vol rallies driven by strike map positioning may be offset by USD-vol correlation in these pairs. Sensitivity is weaker in less-representative pairs: In EM pairs, we find sensitivity is more variable. This may be due to strike maps capturing both lower overall volumes (the positioning score can be more sensitive to one-off flows) and a potentially less-representative share of the overall market in some of these pairs.
